note:
What the last two completed seasons actually taught, drawn from published season reviews rather than from this app's own model.

These are here to be applied, not admired. Each lesson carries a `rule` — the concrete thing it should change about a decision — because a 'lesson' that doesn't change behaviour is a paragraph, not a lesson.

seasons.headline: The season one player broke the game, and being clever cost people their rank.
facts: Salah scored 344 points — an all-time record, beaten by 41 points, and set by Gameweek 28.
Salah's 47 goal involvements (29 goals, 18 assists) drove it.
Mbeumo finished 2nd on 236 points, an improvement of 109 on his previous season.
Isak was the top-scoring forward on 211 points.
Haaland managed 181 points from 31 games — 10 goals in his first six, then three in the next thirteen, plus a spring injury.
Bowen came close to becoming the sixth player ever to reach 200 points.

lessons.lesson: Being slow on the obvious pick was the most expensive mistake of the season.
lessons.detail: Managers who waited on Salah, Isak, Mbeumo and Bowen — all players whose case was already clear — lost more ground than managers who picked a bad differential. The cost of being late on a nailed, in-form, well-priced player compounds every week you delay.
lessons.rule: Never fade a player purely because he is popular. Ownership is not a reason against.

lessons.lesson: Trying too hard to be different is a losing strategy on its own.
lessons.detail: A differential has to be low-owned AND have a credible route to points. Low ownership by itself is not an edge, it is just risk with nobody to share it with.
lessons.rule: Only take a differential when there is a specific structural reason — a role change, a set-piece appointment, a fixture swing.

lessons.detail: Players who reliably play 90 minutes outscored better players who rotated. Minutes are the multiplier on every other statistic in the game.
lessons.rule: Weight expected minutes heavily, and treat a rotation risk as a much bigger discount than it feels like.

seasons.headline: The premium midfield broke, defenders got good, and patience won mini-leagues.
facts: Haaland won the Golden Boot with 27 goals — his third in four seasons — and was the top-scoring outfield player in FPL on 239 points.
He ranked 1st in the entire league for goals (27), shots (126), shots on target (59), xG (27.68) and big chances (51).
Salah collapsed to 116 points; Palmer managed 102. A 34-game indictment of the premium midfielder.
Bowen, Thiago and João Pedro all outscored every premium midfielder except Bruno Fernandes.
Bruno Fernandes won the Playmaker Award with 21 assists.
Gibbs-White scored 188 points at 9.2% ownership — the most efficient differential of the season.
More defenders appeared in the top 50 scorers than the previous year, and fewer midfielders and forwards.

lessons.lesson: The premium midfielder is no longer an automatic buy.
lessons.detail: Two of the three most expensive midfielders in the game returned about 3 points a game across a full season. The money is better spent at the front and the back.
lessons.rule: Build from the front (an elite striker) and the back (a strong defence), and fill midfield with £6-8m players.

lessons.lesson: The £7-8m forward bracket became the strongest position group in the game.
lessons.detail: Mid-price forwards beat premium midfielders outright. That is a structural change in where value sits, not a one-season fluke — it followed the defensive-contributions rule pulling points toward defenders and away from creative midfielders.
lessons.rule: Prefer a £7.5m forward to an £9m midfielder unless the midfielder has penalties or a set-piece monopoly.

lessons.lesson: Defensive contributions changed which defenders are worth owning.
lessons.detail: 10 clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles gets a defender 2 points regardless of the scoreline; midfielders and forwards need 12 including recoveries. Capped at 2 per match. The players who benefit are centre-backs and defensive midfielders — especially at lower and mid-table sides, who defend more because they have less of the ball.
lessons.rule: Value cheap defenders at defensive sides on contribution volume, not only on clean-sheet odds. The ideal profile is contribution volume PLUS clean-sheet potential.

lessons.lesson: Patience with an underowned asset won more than captaincy or chips did.
lessons.detail: The season was not decided by armband calls or chip timing. It was decided by holding 2-3 genuinely good sub-15%-owned players through their quiet weeks instead of churning them.
lessons.rule: Once a differential is bought for a structural reason, hold it through a blank. Selling after two quiet weeks is how a good pick becomes a wasted transfer.

carried_into_2026_27: One gameweek is not a sample. A blank from a proven asset is noise; a haul from an unproven one is a hypothesis, not a fact.
The strongest early-season evidence is structural, not statistical: a confirmed set-piece or penalty appointment, a positional change, a starter ruled out for months.

Haaland has been the top scorer in the game after six gameweeks in all four of his City seasons, averaging nine goals and 61.3 points in that window. Early-season is precisely when fading him is most dangerous.
Defensive contributions continue in 2026/27, so cheap defenders at defensive sides remain live picks.
